_doc: Hand-reviewed verdicts for tools/approach-audit.mjs (history layer v4). `verdicts`: every usable claim of kind movement dated 3 July 1863 or earlier whose printed words name a road, and every arrival_road or march claim that names only a route, with the reason it is not the road of an approach (the builder reads a road of approach from arrival_road and march claims whose printed words name a road; the others were looked at too). `codes`: the text of each code. `for_owner`: claims that came closest and are not used, with the reason, for the Decision Log. The claims of kinds arrival_road and march are reviewed in data/claim-curation.json (approach_exclude); the claims whose road word stands only in the record text around the quote are listed by data/approach-record-scan.json and carry the code record_text_only.

codes.movement_order: a dispatch or an order printed as a movement (what a commander told another to do), not the road a unit marched on to the field
codes.movement_in_field: a move made after the unit stood on the field, or inside it; the road named is where it moved, not the road it came onto the field by
codes.movement_road_unnamed: no road is named: only “the road”, a wrong road, or a direction
codes.movement_wagon_train: a move of the wagon train or its guard; not the approach of the unit's line
codes.movement_black_horse: the road named is the Black Horse Tavern road, which AP-07 prints for the division and which does not cross the loaded ground (no other road is chosen for the unit)
codes.movement_road_not_resolvable: the road named is the “Fairfield road” or the road leading from Gettysburg to Fairfield: two roads of the road layer could carry the name (DEC-007 item 3), so none is chosen
codes.record_text_only: the road word stands only in the report text around the quote (a position beside a road, a camp, a crossing, a line of battle, an earlier leg, an order, or another formation's statement); the claim's own words name no road of approach for this unit (read in full, no approach statement found)
codes.route_not_a_road: the passage names a route by a mill or a village (Horner's Mill), not a road: the repository holds no such road, and none is inferred from the map

notes.POS-C-0027: Barnes's division moved up the Taneytown road between 4 and 6 p. m. on 2 July to the ground Sykes assigned, from the corps's earlier place near the Baltimore pike: a move inside the field after the arrival (the V Corps's road of arrival, the Gettysburg and Hanover road, is printed for the Second Division only, AP-11).
notes.POS-E-US-11C-3D-001: Ledger E (history layer v8): the commission narrative's circuitous route by Horner's Mills for Schurz's and Steinwehr's divisions: a route named by a mill (RC-07), no road
notes.POS-E-US-11C-3D-SCHIMMELFENNIG-45NY-002: Ledger E (history layer v8): 45th NY committee: at or near Horner's Mills, directed by a shorter route to the town: a route, no road named (RC-07)
notes.POS-E-US-11C-3D-SCHIMMELFENNIG-45NY-004: Ledger E (history layer v8): four companies sent out the Mummasburg Road past the College on arrival: a move made inside the field
notes.POS-E-US-11C-3D-SCHIMMELFENNIG-45NY-007: Ledger E (history layer v8): the retreat into the town by the Eagle Hotel and Chambersburg street: a move made inside the field
notes.POS-E-US-11C-3D-KRZYZANOWSKI-58NY-004: Ledger E (history layer v8): with the wagon train from Emmitsburg, road not named; the passage is about the detachment that left the train about four miles out
notes.POS-E-US-11C-ART-1OHI-002: Ledger E (history layer v8): the battery came up Baltimore street in the retreat of 1 July: a move made inside the field
notes.POS-E-US-CAV-1D-DEVIN-17PA-003: Ledger E (history layer v8): a movement on the Harrisburg pike near the town when the Eleventh Corps yielded: a move made inside the field

for_owner.why: arrival_road, Brown (chief of artillery, Second Corps): Jones’ battalion came up “on the York road with Early’s division”; Early prints the Heidlersburg road for the division, which the concordance (RC-01) makes the Harrisburg Road. Two different gazetteer roads for one battalion: both are listed on the card, neither is chosen (approach_block); the owner decides which source to follow.

march, Johnson: “eastwardly, via Scotland, to Gettysburg”. Scotland (Franklin County) is on no period map of the repository (Hopkins covers Adams County only, Warren ends about 5 km west of the borough) and no report names the road between the mountain and the field (RC-05). A research act: a period map of Franklin County or the OR Atlas plate of the route would settle it; the 17 leaf units of Johnson’s division stay open until then.

march, Howard: the Second and Third Divisions took “the route by Horner’s Mill” (13 miles against 10 to 11). A route named by a mill, not a road: no source names the roads of the route or says where it met the road layer (RC-07). Hopkins 1858 prints Horner’s mill about 8 km south of the borough; tracing a route from it would invent the road. A research act (a period map of the Emmitsburg side).
